acpi:SSDT-PCI.aml: OCLP (firmware.py, Sandy and Ivy Bridge Macs): corrects the PCI root bridge resources the firmware reports, so devices behind it get their memory (DSDT error 12 fix)
booter-quirk:AvoidRuntimeDefrag: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): keeps the firmware's runtime services intact while boot.efi lays out memory (non-Apple firmware relies on them after ExitBootServices)
booter-quirk:EnableSafeModeSlide: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): lets boot.efi use the same KASLR slide choice in safe mode as in a normal boot on a non-Apple memory map
booter-quirk:EnableWriteUnprotector: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): lets boot.efi write the pages it must patch where the firmware keeps CR0 write protection on
booter-quirk:FixupAppleEfiImages: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): loads Apple's EFI images on firmware that enforces W^X section rules they don't meet
booter-quirk:ForceBooterSignature: OCLP base: boot.efi sees the firmware's expected booter signature, so the Mac's hibernation and boot-path checks accept OpenCore's boot
booter-quirk:ProtectSecureBoot: OCLP base: boot.efi cannot write Apple Secure Boot variables into this Mac's firmware (protects the NVRAM)
booter-quirk:ProvideCustomSlide: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): picks a KASLR slide that avoids the firmware's reserved regions on a non-Apple memory map, instead of a slide that would fail to boot
booter-quirk:SetupVirtualMap: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): gives the firmware's runtime services a virtual address map, which non-Apple firmware does not set up as Apple's does
kernel-block:com.apple.iokit.IOSkywalkFa: OCLP Wi-Fi (Broadcom on macOS 14+): blocks the OS's IOSkywalkFamily so the injected one (kext:IOSkywalkFamily.kext) loads for the legacy AirPort stack
kernel-patch:Force FileVault on Broken S: OCLP (security.py, SIP lowered): lets FileVault be turned on with the modified (unsealed) System; patches apfs _apfs_filevault_allowed
kernel-patch:IOHIDFamily USB topcase pan: OCLP (misc.py, with AppleUSBTopCase): avoids an IOHIDFamily panic when the legacy USB top-case driver attaches
kernel-patch:Initialize early VM range b: hao kernel repair (kc-binder, kc.bind): the Darwin 27 kernel starts on Ivy Bridge; tests/test_kc_bind.py proves the bytes
kernel-patch:Pass early kernel-map reser: hao kernel repair (kc-binder, kc.bind): Darwin 27 early kernel-map bounds on this Mac; tests/test_kc_bind.py
kernel-patch:Preserve bootstrap physical: hao kernel repair (kc-binder, kc.bind): bootstrap physical-page aliases survive on Ivy Bridge; tests/test_kc_bind.py
hao kernel repair (kc-binder, kc.bind): the registration call of the alias repair; tests/test_kc_bind.py
kernel-patch:hao: hardened programs keep: hao security fix (owner D1, 2026-11-17; src/amfi_dyld.py): with csr-active-config's unrestricted-filesystem bit AMFI counts no program as hardened, so dyld honoured DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES and the other DYLD_* variables in hardened platform programs (measured on 26B131 in hao's stub of /usr/bin/sw_vers, for a user and for root). The patch makes the hardened runtime count inside AMFI's dyld policy only; nothing shipped needs the path (no recipe, launchd job or hao-runtime code sets DYLD_* for a hardened program). Bound per BootKC; tests/test_amfi_dyld.py
kernel-quirk:AppleCpuPmCfgLock: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): skips the CPU power-management MSR writes a firmware with CFG Lock set refuses, which would otherwise panic
kernel-quirk:AppleXcpmCfgLock: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): the same for XCPM on newer CPUs: no write to a locked MSR 0xE2
kernel-quirk:DisableIoMapper: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): macOS ignores the firmware's VT-d (DMAR) tables, which VMs and many PCs present in forms macOS's IOMapper rejects
kernel-quirk:DisableLinkeditJettison: OCLP (build.py, with Lilu): the kernel keeps __LINKEDIT so Lilu and its plug-ins can resolve symbols
kernel-quirk:PanicNoKextDump: OCLP base: a panic report stops after the backtrace instead of listing every kext (readable panic logs)
kernel-quirk:PowerTimeoutKernelPanic: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): a device without a matching driver that misses a power-state deadline is reported instead of panicking the kernel
kernel-quirk:ProvideCurrentCpuInfo: generic image only (opencore-generic, pack generic; from the tested QEMU reference): the kernel gets the CPU's real frequency and core counts on a hypervisor or a CPU it has no table for
kernel-quirk:ThirdPartyDrives: pipeline/targets/mbp92.json third_party_sata_ssd: TRIM for non-Apple SATA SSDs, the drives users fit when they upgrade this Mac (it shipped with an HDD or an Apple SSD); a profile assumption, not a measurement of one laptop
